Vela doğrudan bu cihazdan Google uç noktalarıyla iletişim kurar: hesap yok, takip yok.

Vela’s own place data draws the businesses on the map, so panning around never asks Google, and it works offline. Which places lead is decided by what kind of place they are (hospitals, supermarkets, malls and campuses first), then brand and detail. Searching or tapping a place still goes to Google for hours, reviews and photos.

Google is asked for the places in view every time you pan. Nothing draws offline, and every pan sends your map position to Google. Google’s places are ranked by how many reviews they have, so the busiest name in a plaza takes the label even when it is not the anchor store.

Vela’s data draws the map, and once you stop panning one Google request adds anything it lacks. The extras show online only, and they arrive a beat after the map, so a few icons appear late and can take a label off a neighbor as they land.

Also shows the shops, restaurants and other businesses mapped in OpenStreetMap that Vela’s data lacks. OpenStreetMap edits appear here after the map tiles are rebuilt, usually within a week. On by default.

Tapping a place fetches its hours, reviews and photos from Google, and Vela remembers the match so the next tap is instant. Off = a tapped place shows only what Vela’s data has (name, type, address, phone, website) and nothing about the tap reaches Google. Search and directions still use Google.
Where Vela’s place data comes from

Vela’s place data is Overture Maps, an open dataset of businesses maintained by Meta, Microsoft and others, plus AllThePlaces, which collects chains from their own store locators, with OpenStreetMap correcting where each shop actually sits. Vela bakes the three into map tiles and serves them from its own GitHub repository, so nothing about where you look goes to Meta or Google.nnIt streams in as you browse and downloads with a region for offline use. Where Vela has no data for an area yet, the map falls back to Google.nnSearch, place details, hours, reviews and photos always come from Google, whichever option you pick.
The non-business tier of place icons. Off shows businesses only.

Every couple of minutes during a drive, Vela asks Google for fresh traffic from your current position. That powers faster-route offers and the live arrival time, but it also tells Google where along the route you are. Off: your route still recalculates when you leave it.
Recent searches, recent places, parking history and recorded trips. Saved places and lists stay.
Recent searches, recent places, parking history and every recorded trip will be deleted. This cannot be undone. Saved places and lists are not affected.
Off by default. When on, Vela keeps a short local log you can export and hand to a developer. Nothing is uploaded, and turning it off wipes the log.
Nothing recorded yet. Use the app, then export.

Hides searches, destinations, links and place names from the diagnostics export and rounds its coordinates to about 10 km. Timing, counts and errors stay. Shared trips start on the largest trim distance.

Recorded trips. Tap Replay to play one back on the map (3×):
A recorded drive starts and ends where you do. Trimming deletes every fix near the start, the end, the destination and your Home and Work, keeping the middle at full precision.
Removes %1$d of the recorded points, keeping %2$d. That is %3$d m off the start and %4$d m off the end.
The destination, trip name, spoken directions at either end and the start of the route line go too. Times are rebased so the file does not say when you drove.
First remaining point: %1$s, %2$s. Check it is not somewhere that identifies you.
This drive is shorter than the trim distance, so there is no middle left to share. Try a smaller one.

The trips go out together as one zip file. Each one is trimmed at the same distance: every point near its start, its end, its destination and your Home and Work is deleted, and the middle is kept at full precision.
Trips in the zip: %1$d of %2$d. Points removed: %3$d. Points kept: %4$d.
Left out because they are shorter than the trim distance: %1$d. A smaller distance may keep them.
Every selected trip is shorter than the trim distance, so there is nothing left to share. Try a smaller one.
Name each trip when it is saved
After a recorded drive ends, Vela asks what to call it. Off by default; you can always rename a trip later in the list below.
No trips recorded yet. Navigate somewhere with this on and it’ll show up here to replay.

Vela will record the GPS trace of each navigation on this phone, so a drive can be replayed for testing without driving it again. This is more revealing than diagnostics (it captures your exact routes) but it stays on the phone and is never uploaded. Turn it off any time.
Vela closed unexpectedly recently. Sending the crash report (stack trace) helps fix it. It’s a plain text file, no personal data.
Diagnostics is off, so nothing was recorded leading up to this. Turn it on to capture more detail if it happens again.
Vela will keep a short local log of your searches, routes and any errors. It never leaves the phone unless you tap Export and choose where to send it. Turn it off any time to wipe the log.
Vela is a degoogled maps client: open tiles for the basemap, scraped Google for POIs, routing and traffic-aware ETAs, AOSP TextToSpeech for voice. GPLv3. No Play Services required.

”Take me home” or ”get me to work”
These work spoken or typed into the search bar, in the app language or English. Anything else runs as a normal search.
Turn-by-turn follows you with GPS, which needs precise location. Right now Vela only knows your rough area.
Vela doesn’t have location access. You can allow it in system settings.
Vela only knows your rough area, not where you are. The map shows a wide circle instead of a dot, and turn-by-turn navigation won’t work. You can switch to precise location whenever you want.
Navigation keeps your next turn in a notification, so directions stay with you when the screen is off or you switch apps. Without it, directions only show inside Vela.
That time has passed. Set to now.
Modern matches the Google app’s current palette. Classic is Vela’s earlier look: white roads, yellow motorways, true greens. The two differ most in dark mode right now.

The map, its streets, labels and house numbers are OpenStreetMap data, available under the Open Database License, served as vector tiles by OpenFreeMap. The businesses on the map in covered regions are places data from the Overture Maps Foundation (sourced from Meta and Microsoft), available under the Community Data License Agreement, Permissive 2.0. Place details, reviews, routing and traffic come from Google. Satellite imagery is from Esri and Google.
The button on the map that flips satellite, traffic, transit and terrain.
Crash reports, trips, demo mode, experiments
Light during the day, dark after sunset, worked out from your location.
Keeps your chosen theme everywhere else, and switches by daylight only while you are driving.
Where the name of the road you are on is shown while driving. Above the bar keeps it centered and readable for long names; under the arrow follows the arrow around.
Keeps a button for things that also have a gesture: zoom in and out buttons on the map, and the step list button on the navigation bar. Always on for phones without a touch screen.

When a faster route comes up mid drive, it is taken if you do not answer within a few seconds. Turn this off and an unanswered offer is dismissed instead. Either way the offer never stays on the map waiting.
Pause button on the navigation bar

Puts pause beside the trip figures, where the step list button would be, and leaves mute with the map buttons. Off puts both on one button at the right of the map. Swipe up or use the arrow to open the step list either way.
The step list button has this spot while ”Prefer buttons over swipes” is on, so pause stays with the map buttons.
Keeps the part of the route you have already driven drawn in gray behind the arrow. Off hides it, so only the road ahead is drawn.
Bike routes prefer bike lanes and quiet streets

Cycling routes favour signed cycle routes, bike lanes and residential streets over the fastest road, the way Google routes bikes. Uses the offline map where you have one downloaded, otherwise an open router online. Off gives the plain fastest bike route.
Shows one route at a time, with the others behind a tap and their times on the map, and Start along the bottom. Turn it off for Vela’s classic panel, which lists every route at once.

A strip beside the map showing traffic and what is coming up on the rest of your route. Shows only what Vela actually knows: congestion, lights, stop signs, level crossings, speed bumps and surveillance cameras. Portrait only.
Vela cannot ship Google Sans: it is proprietary and cannot be redistributed. You can point Vela at any font file on your own device instead. Map labels keep their own font.
